name: gizza-ai/article-to-epub
summary: Package article text or cleaned HTML into a valid EPUB ebook

tool.description: Package an article — plain text or cleaned HTML — into a valid EPUB 3 ebook and return it as a download. Sets the title, author, language and publisher metadata, splits chapters at headings, builds both an EPUB 3 nav document and an EPUB 2 NCX table of contents, and embeds a reading stylesheet. Messy HTML is re-emitted as well-formed XHTML with scripts, styles and forms removed; images are not packaged (their alt text is kept).

author.description: Author for dc:creator, e.g. 'Jane Doe'. Empty omits the element.

base_font_size.description: Base font size in points for the embedded stylesheet, e.g. 12. 0 (default) leaves the size to the reading app, which is what most e-readers expect.

content.description: The article itself: plain text or cleaned HTML. Plain text uses blank lines for paragraphs and understands Markdown-style '# ' headings, '-' bullets and '1.' lists. HTML is re-emitted as well-formed XHTML; scripts, styles and forms are dropped.

include_title_page.description: Write a title page with the title, author and publisher as the first page of the book (default true).

input_format.description:
How to read the content. 'auto' (default) detects HTML by looking for tags like

or

; set 'html' or 'text' to force it (use 'text' to keep angle brackets in prose literal).

language.description: Book language as a BCP-47 tag for dc:language, e.g. 'en', 'de' or 'pt-BR' (default 'en').

publisher.description: Publisher or source name for dc:publisher, e.g. the site the article came from. Empty omits the element.

split_level.description: Where a new chapter starts: 'h1' (default), 'h2', 'h1-h2' for both, or 'none' for one single chapter. Chapter titles become the table of contents.

title.description: Book title (dc:title) and the download filename. Leave empty to derive it from the HTML <title>, the first heading, or the first line of text.
